title: Term Life Insurance Grace Period and Lapse Provision
content:
## Provision

When an installment is unpaid on its due date — the paid-to date — a Term Life Insurance policy enters the grace period and coverage continues. The grace period lasts the product's grace period days, except that a policy whose issue state appears in the product's state list uses the number of days listed for that state.

The overdue premium must be received no later than the last day of the grace period, which is the unpaid installment's due date plus the grace period days. The last day of grace is found by adding the grace period length in calendar days to the due date; a remittance received on that day is in time. The clock starts from the unpaid installment's due date, as shown by the paid-to date on the policy record, and the grace length follows the issue state on that record.

The clause "when every overdue installment is paid in time the policy returns to in force" is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current basis.

If the grace period ends with premium still due, the policy lapses: the lapse date is the day after the last day of grace, coverage ends, and term coverage has no cash value or nonforfeiture benefit. A death during the grace period is covered and the overdue installments are deducted from the proceeds.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, 31-day grace)

| Paid-to date (due date) | Last day of grace | Remittance received | In time? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 March | 1 April | 1 April | yes — received on the last day |
| 1 March | 1 April | 2 April | no — the policy lapsed; lapse date 2 April |

For a policy issued in a state listed with 60 days, the same due date of 1 March gives a last day of grace of 30 April.

## Points of judgement

- Calendar days are counted, not business days.
- The lapse date is the first day without coverage, the day after the last day of grace.
